card.title: KAWASAKI Ki-10
card.text: Gets +1 attack until end of turn after you attack with a Japanese unit.
card.flavorText: The Kawasaki Ki-10 was the last biplane fighter used by the Imperial Japanese Army. Designed by Takeo Doi, it entered service in 1935 and served during Japan’s early campaigns in China. A total of 588 units were produced. Though technically outdated compared to contemporary monoplanes, the Army favored the Ki-10 for its agility and handling, especially in dogfighting. The aircraft featured unequal-span biplane wings with a fabric-covered metal frame and was powered by an 850 hp Kawasaki Ha9-IIa V-12 engine. It was armed with two forward-firing 7.7 mm Type 89 machine guns and could reach a top speed of 400 km/h. Several variants were developed, with the Ki-10-II offering aerodynamic improvements and a slightly modified engine. In combat, the Ki-10 saw action in Manchukuo and during the early stages of the Second Sino-Japanese War. It was involved in escort and interception missions, notably during bombing raids over Taiyuan in 1937. It became largely obsolete by 1939, and was replaced by the more modern Ki-27, though the Ki-10 remained in service for training and patrol duties until early 1942.
